records.distinguishing_traits_text: Heritable information; metabolism; evolutionary descent
records.evolutionary_history_text: All known cellular organisms share ancestral biochemical systems. Oldest evidence of life is debated, with multiple geochemical and stromatolite lines of evidence.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Prokaryotic organization; diverse cell envelopes; extraordinary metabolic breadth
records.evolutionary_history_text: Bacteria are one of three major cellular domains; metabolism reshaped Earth long before animal life.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Distinct membrane lipids; archaeal information processing; diverse chemistries
records.evolutionary_history_text: Archaea include methanogens, salt-tolerant groups and lineages closely related to eukaryotes. Deep branching remains actively revised.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Nucleus; endomembranes; mitochondria or descendants; cytoskeleton
records.evolutionary_history_text: Eukaryotic cellular complexity arose through symbiogenesis and gene exchange; multicellularity arose independently several times.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Bacterial ribosomes; varied respiration and photosynthesis; rapid horizontal gene transfer
records.evolutionary_history_text: Bacterial metabolisms include oxygenic photosynthesis, nitrogen fixation, sulfate reduction, and aerobic respiration.
records.original_diversity_or_population_text: Tens of thousands formally named species

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Ether-linked membrane lipids in many; archaea-specific molecular machineries; methanogenesis in some
records.evolutionary_history_text: Archaea occupy terrestrial, marine, host-associated, and high-temperature habitats, not only extremes.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Ancestral single posterior flagellum; shared molecular synapomorphies
records.evolutionary_history_text: This evolutionary branch includes animal and fungal ancestors, with important single-celled relatives not fully shown in the atlas.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Primary plastids derived from cyanobacteria; photosynthetic lineages
records.evolutionary_history_text: Primary plastid endosymbiosis enabled the evolution of red algae, green plants, and glaucophytes.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Plastids; cellulose-rich cell walls; photosynthesis; alternating generations in land plants
records.evolutionary_history_text: Green plant ancestry lies among freshwater-related green algal lines; land colonization reshaped soils, weathering, and atmospheric carbon. Circumscription of Plantae varies.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Absorptive nutrition; chitin-rich walls in many; hyphal networks common
records.evolutionary_history_text: Fungi evolved potent extracellular digestion, mineral uptake and symbioses; mycorrhizal partnerships aided land plants.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Many with complex plastids; diverse flagella; marine primary production
records.evolutionary_history_text: Chromista is a classification-dependent assemblage. Its boundaries and monophyly are debated; many lineages arose through complex plastid symbiosis.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Mostly unicellular eukaryotes; phagocytosis in many; diverse motility
records.evolutionary_history_text: Traditional Protozoa is paraphyletic: organisms grouped under it do not form one exclusive evolutionary branch. Shown as a historical taxonomic category.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Oxygenic photosynthesis; chlorophyll a; thylakoids in many
records.evolutionary_history_text: Cyanobacterial oxygen production helped drive the Great Oxidation Event; a cyanobacterium became the ancestor of plastids.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Heterocysts in many; nitrogen fixation; filaments
records.evolutionary_history_text: Some members specialize cells to fix nitrogen while neighboring cells produce oxygen.

records.etymology: Traditional name applied to gelatinous colonies
records.distinguishing_traits_text: Gelatinous colonies; heterocysts in many
records.evolutionary_history_text: Nostoc species inhabit soils, rock surfaces and freshwater, often responding to periodic wetting.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Nitrogen-fixing colonies; desiccation tolerance
records.evolutionary_history_text: Visible gelatinous colonies expand rapidly after rain.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Diverse Gram-negative lineages; photosynthesis or heterotrophy
records.evolutionary_history_text: Includes many symbionts, marine bacteria, soil organisms and pathogens.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Highly varied respiratory and ecological strategies
records.evolutionary_history_text: Includes enteric bacteria, vibrios, and many marine groups.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Facultative anaerobes common
records.evolutionary_history_text: Includes abundant gut-associated and environmental species.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Gram-negative rods; fermentative capacity in many
records.evolutionary_history_text: Contains model organisms and pathogenic relatives.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Facultatively anaerobic enteric organisms
records.evolutionary_history_text: E. coli became a central model for molecular genetics and microbial ecology.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Enormous strain diversity; adaptable metabolism
records.evolutionary_history_text: Most strains inhabit vertebrate guts without causing disease, while certain lineages are pathogenic.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Many Gram-positive lineages; spore formation in some
records.evolutionary_history_text: Important decomposers, gut symbionts, fermenters, and pathogens.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Some form endospores
records.evolutionary_history_text: Contains Bacillus and relatives adapted to contrasting habitats.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Aerobic and facultative taxa; endospores in some
records.evolutionary_history_text: Includes soil-adapted bacterial lineages.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Bacterial spores in many members
records.evolutionary_history_text: Common in soils and other terrestrial habitats.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Resistant endospores
records.evolutionary_history_text: Includes widely studied soil microorganisms.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Sporulation; biofilm formation; competence
records.evolutionary_history_text: A classic bacterium for studying cellular differentiation and gene regulation.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Methanogenesis in several lineages; halophiles
records.evolutionary_history_text: Traditional Euryarchaeota membership is heavily revised in newer phylogenomic systems.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Methanogenesis; hydrogen metabolism
records.evolutionary_history_text: Methane production is an ancient biological source of atmospheric methane.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Hydrogenotrophic methane production common
records.evolutionary_history_text: Grow in anaerobic environments, including animal digestive systems.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Methane-producing metabolism
records.evolutionary_history_text: A group involved in anoxic carbon cycling.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Often host-associated
records.evolutionary_history_text: Some species inhabit mammal intestines.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Hydrogen-consuming methanogenesis
records.evolutionary_history_text: Common archaeal member of human gut microbiomes.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Many heat-adapted members; archaeal cell biology
records.evolutionary_history_text: Contains branches formerly placed within Crenarchaeota; broader modern usage varies.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Acidothermal adaptations in many
records.evolutionary_history_text: Diverse archaea thrive in sulfur-rich hot springs.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Thermoacidophily common
records.evolutionary_history_text: Oxidize sulfur compounds in acidic thermal environments.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Extremophilic cell membranes
records.evolutionary_history_text: Important models for archaeal molecular biology.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Thermoacidophilic growth
records.evolutionary_history_text: Thermoacidophiles found in geothermal areas.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Grows at high temperature and low pH
records.evolutionary_history_text: A model for archaeal chromosomal replication and cellular division.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Gametophyte-dominant; spores; no true vascular tissue
records.evolutionary_history_text: Early land plants helped establish terrestrial habitats, while moss lineages retained a dominant gametophyte.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Water-holding cells; peat formation
records.evolutionary_history_text: Peat mosses influence carbon storage and wetland acidity.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Acidifying growth; high water retention
records.evolutionary_history_text: Sphagnum plants create waterlogged peatlands with slow decomposition.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Wetland moss
records.evolutionary_history_text: Peatland moss distributed across broad temperate areas.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Xylem and phloem; lignified support; sporophyte dominance
records.evolutionary_history_text: Transport and structural tissues enabled taller terrestrial growth and diverse vascular ecologies.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Fronds; spores; vascular tissue
records.evolutionary_history_text: Ferns diversified extensively in humid terrestrial settings and persist globally.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Often upright trunks; large fronds
records.evolutionary_history_text: Tree ferns were conspicuous in many Mesozoic forests.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Pollen and ovules; seed development
records.evolutionary_history_text: Seeds freed reproduction from surface-water dependence and protected embryos.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Cones; pollen; wood; many evergreen leaves
records.evolutionary_history_text: Conifers dominate important high-latitude and montane forests.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Needle or scale leaves; naked ovules
records.evolutionary_history_text: Conifers occupied diverse Mesozoic habitats before flowering plant radiation.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Seed-bearing woody plants
records.evolutionary_history_text: Includes many living conifer families.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Resin canals; woody cones
records.evolutionary_history_text: Includes pines, spruces, firs, and larches.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Needles in fascicles in many
records.evolutionary_history_text: Pines are important fire- and drought-adapted trees.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Conifer with needle fascicles
records.evolutionary_history_text: Widespread Eurasian tree adapted to cool climates.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Flowers; enclosed seeds; double fertilization
records.evolutionary_history_text: Flowering plants radiated during the Cretaceous alongside pollinators and herbivores.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Tricolpate pollen in core eudicots
records.evolutionary_history_text: A large flowering plant lineage; class circumscription differs by system.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Diverse flowers and fruits
records.evolutionary_history_text: An important angiosperm order occupying many habitats.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Hypanthium in many; diverse fruits
records.evolutionary_history_text: Contains roses, apples, pears, cherries, and strawberries.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Prickles in many; fragrant flowers
records.evolutionary_history_text: Wild roses occupy temperate regions worldwide.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Pink flowers; vitamin-rich hips
records.evolutionary_history_text: A wild rose native to Europe, northwest Africa, and western Asia.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Asci and ascospores; diverse yeast and filament forms
records.evolutionary_history_text: Ascomycetes include lichens, decomposers, crop pathogens, and baking yeasts.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Single-celled budding forms common
records.evolutionary_history_text: Fermentation made budding yeasts major partners of humans.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Many sugar-fermenting yeasts
records.evolutionary_history_text: This order includes laboratory and industrial yeasts.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Fermentative metabolic diversity
records.evolutionary_history_text: Yeasts adapted to fruit and other sugar-rich environments.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Alcoholic fermentation
records.evolutionary_history_text: Used to study genetics, aging, and basic cell biology.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Unicellular eukaryote; budding; fermentation
records.evolutionary_history_text: A model eukaryote with an extensively studied genome and cell cycle.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Basidia bearing sexual spores; mushrooms in many
records.evolutionary_history_text: Major wood-decaying fungi, mushrooms, rusts and smuts.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Complex fruiting bodies in many
records.evolutionary_history_text: Includes gilled mushrooms, bracket fungi and puffballs.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Gills or transformed spore-bearing structures
records.evolutionary_history_text: Includes edible and poisonous mushrooms.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Veils and gill-bearing fruiting bodies in many
records.evolutionary_history_text: Contains edible cultivated mushrooms and their relatives.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Fleshy fruiting bodies; dark mature gills
records.evolutionary_history_text: Includes the domesticated button mushroom.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Often two-spored basidia
records.evolutionary_history_text: Widely farmed as white button, cremini, and portobello mushrooms.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Chlorophyll c; fucoxanthin in many
records.evolutionary_history_text: Photosynthetic lineages are central to marine food webs and global carbon cycling.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Fucoxanthin; multicellularity; alginate walls
records.evolutionary_history_text: Kelp forests form productive temperate coastal ecosystems.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Large blades; holdfasts; underwater canopies
records.evolutionary_history_text: Kelp forests buffer waves and support diverse marine species.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Stipes, blades, and holdfasts
records.evolutionary_history_text: Giant brown algae in temperate seas.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Ribbonlike blades
records.evolutionary_history_text: Important habitat formers on rocky coasts.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Finger-like blade divisions
records.evolutionary_history_text: Common in rocky North Atlantic coastal zones.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Silica frustules; photosynthetic unicells
records.evolutionary_history_text: Diatoms produce substantial marine and freshwater primary productivity.
records.original_diversity_or_population_text: Tens of thousands of named species

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Cellulose-rich walls in many; diploid dominant; swimming spores
records.evolutionary_history_text: Oomycetes resemble fungi but are evolutionarily distinct; many are plant pathogens.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Plant pathogenicity; zoospores
records.evolutionary_history_text: Includes organisms responsible for major crop diseases.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Oomycete crop pathogen
records.evolutionary_history_text: A principal cause of devastating potato blights, including the Irish Great Famine.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Lobose pseudopodia in many; phagocytosis
records.evolutionary_history_text: An important eukaryotic lineage, though the taxonomic Protozoa umbrella is not a true clade.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Tubular pseudopodia
records.evolutionary_history_text: Amoebas change shape to feed and migrate.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Pseudopods; phagocytosis
records.evolutionary_history_text: Amoebas have served as classic models for cell motility.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Large lobose pseudopodia
records.evolutionary_history_text: A widely used teaching organism in cell biology.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Flagellates; diverse feeding strategies; crystalline rods
records.evolutionary_history_text: Some members photosynthesize; others are parasites or free-living heterotrophs.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Distinct kinetoplast mitochondrial DNA
records.evolutionary_history_text: Includes disease-causing trypanosomes and free-living relatives.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Flagellated protists; complex parasite cycles
records.evolutionary_history_text: Trypanosomes evolved intricate host-vector life cycles.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Variant surface glycoproteins; antigenic variation
records.evolutionary_history_text: A parasite transmitted by tsetse flies that can cause human African trypanosomiasis.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Cilia; nuclear dimorphism in many
records.evolutionary_history_text: Ciliates have specialized feeding apparatus and dual nuclear systems.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Coordinated ciliary currents
records.evolutionary_history_text: Includes major protist laboratory models.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Cilia; contractile vacuoles
records.evolutionary_history_text: Classic freshwater protists with sophisticated ciliary coordination.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Elongated body; oral groove
records.evolutionary_history_text: A familiar protist viewed in microscope ponds samples.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Multicellularity; developmental gene networks; extracellular collagen; heterotrophy
records.evolutionary_history_text: Animals emerged among marine eukaryotes during the Neoproterozoic. Body plans diversified dramatically across the Ediacaran–Cambrian transition; fossil and molecular clocks do not agree on a single origin date.
records.original_diversity_or_population_text: 1,796,900 species listed in Catalogue of Life (Sept 2026 XR)

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Eight rows of ciliary comb plates; prey-capturing colloblasts; diffuse nerve net
records.evolutionary_history_text: A proposed earliest-diverging animal lineage based on synteny data. Whether it or sponges branch first remains contested; neural origins are consequently debated.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Choanocyte filter feeding; porous aquiferous canals; spicules / spongin
records.evolutionary_history_text: Sponge-like remains may predate the Cambrian, but the oldest fossil assignments are disputed. Most lack organized nerves, muscles and a conventional gut.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Flattened ciliated body; very few cell types; no neurons
records.evolutionary_history_text: Tiny creeping marine animals that illuminate early animal tissue evolution; relationships to cnidarians and bilaterians remain under study.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Shared developmental regulators; increasingly complex epithelia
records.evolutionary_history_text: A proposed group generally including Placozoa, Cnidaria and Bilateria, though some deep relationships remain debated.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Cnidocytes with stinging organelles; gastrovascular cavity; radial tendencies
records.evolutionary_history_text: Cnidarians evolved specialized nerve nets and stinging cells. Many reef builders shaped Paleozoic and later seas.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Polyp-only adult; many photosymbioses; reef construction
records.evolutionary_history_text: Scleractinian corals radiated especially from the Triassic onward after earlier reef systems collapsed.

records.etymology: Medusa, Greek mythological name for the jellyfish stage
records.distinguishing_traits_text: Many life cycles include medusae; specialized sensory structures
records.evolutionary_history_text: Gelatinous predators evolved diverse pulsating medusae and sessile stages.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Anteroposterior polarity; mesoderm; bilateral ancestry
records.evolutionary_history_text: Bilaterians probably originated in the Ediacaran; many recognizable body plans become abundant in the Cambrian. A number of descendants later evolved radial symmetry.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Diverse neural and embryological patterns; ecdysozoan and spiralian branches
records.evolutionary_history_text: Includes arthropods, mollusks, annelids and many worm phyla. The old “mouth-first” rule has exceptions and does not diagnose every species.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Some branches with spiral cleavage; diverse larval forms
records.evolutionary_history_text: Includes mollusks, annelids and flatworms. Not all spiralians retain spiral cleavage.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Mantle; muscular foot (often modified); radula in many groups
records.evolutionary_history_text: An exceptionally varied Cambrian-origin group; shells fossilize readily, leaving rich records of Paleozoic–Cenozoic oceans.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Embryonic torsion; diverse shells or shell loss; aquatic and terrestrial habits
records.evolutionary_history_text: Gastropods radiated across marine, freshwater and terrestrial environments.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Two hinged shells; filter-feeding gills in most; no radula
records.evolutionary_history_text: Bivalves became major marine filter feeders and expanded ecologically during Mesozoic diversification.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Arms/tentacles around head; advanced eyes and behavior; jet propulsion
records.evolutionary_history_text: Once represented by abundant shelled forms; coleoid cephalopods subsequently diversified high-performance locomotion and nervous systems.

records.etymology: Ammon, Egyptian deity depicted with ram horns
records.distinguishing_traits_text: Chambered coiled shell; complex sutures in many groups
records.evolutionary_history_text: Ammonoids evolved in the Devonian, recovered after several mass extinctions, and disappeared at the end-Cretaceous extinction.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Internalized/reduced shells; chromatophores; complex learning
records.evolutionary_history_text: Squids, cuttlefish and octopuses evolved rapid camouflage and large centralized brains.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Eight sucker-bearing arms; shell highly reduced or absent; dexterity
records.evolutionary_history_text: Octopuses evolved unusually distributed nervous systems and sophisticated object manipulation.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Three hearts; arm-local circuitry; rapid skin-pattern control
records.evolutionary_history_text: A modern shallow-water octopus complex; some populations historically assigned to this name represent other species.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Serially repeated segments; chaetae in many; hydrostatic support
records.evolutionary_history_text: Marine worms were important Cambrian sediment mixers; earthworms later helped reshape soils.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Clitellum for reproduction; direct development common
records.evolutionary_history_text: A mostly freshwater and terrestrial diversification of annelid worms.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Dorsoventrally flat; no coelom; many parasitic taxa
records.evolutionary_history_text: Includes free-living planarians and multiple independently diverse parasitic lineages.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Ecdysis / molting of an external cuticle
records.evolutionary_history_text: A molecularly supported group uniting arthropods, roundworms, tardigrades and velvet worms.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Collagenous molted cuticle; pseudocoelom; longitudinal muscles
records.evolutionary_history_text: Highly abundant in many soils and sediments; some species are parasitic or key laboratory models.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Segmented appendages; molting; distinct limb specializations
records.evolutionary_history_text: Cambrian lobopodian fossils illuminate the evolution of articulated limbs.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Four pairs of lobopod legs; cryptobiosis in many species
records.evolutionary_history_text: Some tolerate desiccation by entering a tun state; they are not universally resistant to all extremes.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Soft lobopod legs; adhesive slime jets; tracheae
records.evolutionary_history_text: Living velvet worms preserve combinations of features helpful for interpreting Cambrian panarthropods.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Jointed appendages; chitinous exoskeleton; segmented body
records.evolutionary_history_text: Most described animal species are arthropods. Their Cambrian ancestors diversified in seas before insects colonized land and air.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Three longitudinal lobes; many mineralized dorsal segments
records.evolutionary_history_text: Iconic Paleozoic marine arthropods, extinct at the end-Permian extinction. Not direct ancestors of modern insects.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Chelicerae feeding appendages; no antennae
records.evolutionary_history_text: Marine ancestors gave rise to extensive terrestrial arachnid radiations.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Four pairs of walking legs in adult typical forms; chelicerae
records.evolutionary_history_text: Arachnids are major terrestrial predators, parasites and soil inhabitants.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Spinnerets producing silk; venomous fangs in most
records.evolutionary_history_text: Spider silk and aerial prey capture diversified through the Mesozoic.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Mandibles derived from modified appendages
records.evolutionary_history_text: Unites myriapods and pancrustaceans; several deep relationships remain under revision.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Many trunk segments; terrestrial life
records.evolutionary_history_text: Early land arthropods included myriapod relatives adapting to oxygen-rich terrestrial microhabitats.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Molecularly supported clade that nests hexapods within crustacean-grade ancestors
records.evolutionary_history_text: “Crustacea” excluding insects is paraphyletic; this tree keeps insects and other crustaceans together.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Characteristically 19 segments; specialized thoracic limbs
records.evolutionary_history_text: Crabs, lobsters and shrimp have repeatedly occupied strikingly different marine and freshwater niches.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Five pairs of thoracic walking limbs
records.evolutionary_history_text: Decapods became major marine scavengers, predators and ecosystem engineers.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Six walking legs on thorax; land adaptations
records.evolutionary_history_text: Hexapods originated on land and subsequently evolved wings in the insect lineage.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Head, thorax and abdomen; three leg pairs; wings in most lineages
records.evolutionary_history_text: The largest described animal class; winged insects later drove terrestrial pollination and food webs.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Larva, pupa and adult; distinct feeding niches
records.evolutionary_history_text: Complete metamorphosis helped beetles, butterflies, flies and bees partition ecological roles.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Protective hardened elytra over hindwings
records.evolutionary_history_text: Beetles diversified alongside plants, wood decomposers and other ecosystems.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Scale-covered wings; coiled proboscis in many adults
records.evolutionary_history_text: Lepidopteran diversification closely interacted with flowering plants during the Cretaceous and Cenozoic.

records.etymology: Danaus, Greek mythic king; plexippus, mythological personal name
records.distinguishing_traits_text: Toxic milkweed diet; long-distance multigenerational migration
records.evolutionary_history_text: The North American migratory populations depend on milkweed breeding habitat and overwintering forests.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Hook-linked membranous wings in most; parasitoidism and eusociality
records.evolutionary_history_text: Several eusocial lineages evolved complex division of labor and sophisticated collective behavior.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: One flying wing pair; balancing halteres
records.evolutionary_history_text: Dipterans diversified as pollinators, decomposers and some major disease vectors.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Includes echinoderms and chordates; multiple embryo-development patterns
records.evolutionary_history_text: The name refers to an embryological generalization with exceptions; fossil representatives appear by the Cambrian.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Water vascular system; calcitic endoskeleton; secondary pentaradial symmetry
records.evolutionary_history_text: Cambrian stem forms reveal the transition from bilaterian ancestors to characteristic adult radial plans.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Tube feet; regenerative arms; usually five rays
records.evolutionary_history_text: Sea stars evolved diverse predatory feeding strategies in benthic marine habitats.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Fused test plates; movable spines; Aristotle’s lantern in most
records.evolutionary_history_text: Regular echinoids diversified in the Paleozoic; irregular echinoids radiated in Mesozoic seas.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Notochord; dorsal hollow nerve cord; pharyngeal openings; postanal tail at some stage
records.evolutionary_history_text: Cambrian fossils preserve chordate-like and vertebrate-like animals. Tunicates and vertebrates are close relatives.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Larval notochord; cellulose-like tunic in adults
records.evolutionary_history_text: Genomic evidence places tunicates as the living sister lineage to vertebrates.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Specialized cranium; vertebral elements in most; neural crest
records.evolutionary_history_text: Early vertebrates were jawless marine animals; jawed lineages later radiated on reefs and beyond.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Cartilage-dominant skeleton; tooth replacement; electroreception in many
records.evolutionary_history_text: Cartilaginous fish radiated from Paleozoic jawed-vertebrate ancestors.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Endochondral bone; lungs or swim bladder ancestrally
records.evolutionary_history_text: Cladistically includes all tetrapods: humans are deeply nested within bony vertebrates.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Fin rays supported by dermal skeleton
records.evolutionary_history_text: Teleosts underwent a major Mesozoic–Cenozoic diversification in fresh and marine waters.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Paired fleshy fins/limbs with internal bones
records.evolutionary_history_text: The lineages of coelacanths and lungfish diverged from the ancestor that also led to land vertebrates.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Digit-bearing limbs ancestrally; air breathing and modified senses
records.evolutionary_history_text: Originated from Devonian sarcopterygian ancestry; some descendants later lost limbs or returned to water.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Permeable skin; often aquatic larval stage; diverse reproduction
records.evolutionary_history_text: Modern amphibians radiated after early tetrapod lineages, with a fossil record extending into the Paleozoic.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Amniotic membranes; reproduction less tied to standing water
records.evolutionary_history_text: The amniotic egg enabled major diversification on land during the Carboniferous and Permian.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Single ancestral lower temporal skull opening
records.evolutionary_history_text: Includes Permian sail-backed forms, therapsids and living mammals. Many early synapsids are not true mammals.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Mammary glands; hair; three middle-ear ossicles
records.evolutionary_history_text: Crown mammals originated by the Mesozoic and radiated extensively after the K–Pg extinction.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Egg laying; milk secretion without nipples
records.evolutionary_history_text: Surviving egg-laying mammals from an ancient mammalian divergence.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Shared reproductive and skeletal traits
records.evolutionary_history_text: Unites marsupials and placentals; deep lineages diverged in Mesozoic time.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Short gestation in many species; prolonged lactation
records.evolutionary_history_text: Marsupial evolutionary history spans South America, Antarctica and Australia.

records.distinguishing_traits_text: Extended gestation with complex chorioallantoic placenta
